# Results — Study 666 (McClellan Summation Index)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The believers' claim — **the
McClellan Summation Index (the running cumulative sum of the McClellan Oscillator, study
[491](../../491-mcclellan-oscillator/)) times bull/bear regimes: crossing zero confirms a
new market phase, and extreme excursions (classically ±500/±1000 on the full-NYSE scale)
mark overbought/oversold turning points** — encoded as a mechanical rule three ways: the raw
zero-cross, a scale-appropriate causal z-score analog of the ±500 level, and a long/flat
regime timer. Offline & deterministic once cached; run `python examples/verify.py` to
reproduce every number. As-of **2026-06-30** (the last complete calendar month).*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance daily adjusted (**total-return**) closes; traded instrument **SPY**, 2005-01-04 → 2026-06-30 (public, no key) |
| Breadth proxy | daily **net advances** = (# basket members up) − (# down) across `['SPY','XLK','XLF','XLE','XLV','XLI','XLY','XLP','XLU','XLB']` (SPY + the 9 classic SPDR sector ETFs, live since 1998) — a **coarse proxy** for true NYSE exchange breadth (thousands of issues); identical basket to sibling [491-mcclellan-oscillator](../../491-mcclellan-oscillator/) so the two studies' breadth inputs are directly comparable |
| Window | 5,405 sessions, 2005-01-04 → 2026-06-30 (**21.4 years**); 19.5 years remain after the burn-in |
| SPY fingerprint | `8266ce2012be` (sha1[:12] of the as-of-sliced close column) |
| Breadth fingerprint | `d10dadd9e2b7` (sha1[:12] of the as-of-sliced net-advances column) |
| Indicator | Summation Index = cumsum(EMA₁₉(net_adv) − EMA₃₉(net_adv)), causal, never re-based |
| Timing / costs | events entered at the **next close** (one documented lag); event study 1 bp one-way × 2 legs; regime timer 5 bps one-way × NAV per regime switch, regime read at close *t-1* applied to day *t* |
| Survivorship | **None on the Signal axis.** SPY and the 9 sector SPDRs are the actual traded universe throughout 2005→2026 — no membership changes, no delisted names dropped, unlike an index-constituent panel |
| Warm-up (named quirk) | the un-rebased cumulative sum has no natural zero — it is started at 0 on the basket's first session and never re-based. **500 sessions (~2 years) are dropped** as burn-in before any statistic is computed (`WARMUP_DAYS` in `strategy.py`) |

## The headline — the textbook zero-cross regime signal is structurally inert

| quantity | value |
|---|---|
| Summation Index range, full sample | **[0.00, 128.45]** |
| raw zero-**up**-crosses, no warm-up filter | **1** (on 2005-01-06 — day 2 of the basket's history) |
| raw zero-**down**-crosses, no warm-up filter | **0**, ever, in 21.4 years |
| zero-up-crosses **after** the 500-session burn-in | **0** |
| zero-down-crosses **after** the 500-session burn-in | **0** |

The finding is not a coding artefact: **the Summation Index never revisits zero after its
first week of history.** The 10-name basket's net advances carries a persistent positive
mean (equities close up more sessions than down, on average, over a two-decade bull-biased
window), so the un-rebased running sum climbs to a range of roughly [83, 128] within the
first few months and then oscillates *inside that range* for 21 years — never once dipping
back to zero, let alone below it. **The textbook "crosses up/down through zero" regime
signal — the claim's central mechanism — cannot fire even once on this real tape.** This
holds across every EMA-span and basket variant we tried (see Robustness below): 0 crosses,
always.

## Extreme-threshold events — a scale-appropriate ±500 analog, tested against random days

The literature's ±500/±1000 levels are calibrated to full-NYSE-exchange net-advances counts
(thousands of issues) and do not transfer numerically to a 10-name ETF proxy. We use a
**causal, rolling 252-session z-score** of the Summation Index (no look-ahead — each day's z
uses only its own trailing window) and treat a ±1σ cross as the scale-appropriate analog of
the literature's extreme level, entered at the next close (one lag), forward returns vs a
drift-matched random-entry baseline (Welch *t*):

**Up-cross (z > +1, "extreme bullish breadth"), n = 45**

| horizon | trigger | one-sample *t* | random | delta | Welch *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 5d  | +14.7 bps  | +0.94 | −24.4 bps | +39.2 bps  | +0.78 |
| 10d | +30.8 bps  | +1.06 | +11.9 bps | +18.9 bps  | +0.27 |
| 20d | +128.1 bps | +3.02 | +125.7 bps | +2.5 bps  | +0.03 |
| 60d | +240.7 bps | +2.85 | +564.6 bps | **−323.9 bps** | **−2.50** |

**Down-cross (z < −1, "extreme bearish breadth"), n = 43**

| horizon | trigger | one-sample *t* | random | delta | Welch *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 5d  | +24.1 bps  | +0.56 | −24.4 bps | +48.5 bps | +0.74 |
| 10d | −10.7 bps  | −0.17 | +11.9 bps | −22.7 bps | −0.24 |
| 20d | +134.6 bps | +1.44 | +125.7 bps | +8.9 bps  | +0.08 |
| 60d | +492.0 bps | +4.00 | +564.6 bps | −72.6 bps | −0.45 |

The one-sample *t*'s look respectable (up to +4.00 at 60d) — but that is **pure beta**: any
long window on a 21-year, mostly-rising SPY tape inherits the drift, and the *random-day*
baseline shows the same or larger mean. Against the drift-matched random baseline, **7 of 8
direction × horizon Welch *t*'s are indistinguishable from noise**; the one exception (60d
up-cross, *t* = −2.50) is *negative* — the **wrong sign** for the claim ("extreme bullish
breadth forecasts a rally"), and is exactly the false-positive rate you'd expect sweeping
8 comparisons. No coherent, correctly-signed edge survives the random-day control.

**Shuffled-breadth placebo** (extreme up-cross, H=20d, time-permute `net_adv`, rebuild the
Summation Index, re-fire the cross, 500 draws): observed **+128.1 bps** vs **p = 0.309** —
scrambling the breadth series' temporal structure while keeping its marginal distribution
leaves the up-cross return statistically unremarkable. The specific EMA19−EMA39-then-cumsum
geometry carries no information beyond its marginal.

## The long/flat regime timer — the headline tradability test

Hold SPY while the Summation Index sits in its "bull" regime, flat otherwise; one execution
lag (yesterday's close regime sets today's exposure); 5 bps one-way × NAV per switch.

| regime rule | switches (21.4y) | frac. long | timed CAGR | buy&hold CAGR | excess (bps/day) | HAC *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| textbook: Summ > 0 | **0** | 100% | +10.90% | +10.90% | 0.000 | n/a (identical to buy&hold) |
| adapted: Summ > its trailing 1y mean (z > 0) | **115** (5.9/yr) | 53% | **+3.95%** | +10.90% | **−3.125** | **−2.43** |

Because the raw zero level never crosses (above), the textbook rule is a silent,
permanent buy-and-hold in disguise — it holds no information about regimes at all on this
tape. The **scale-adapted** rule (bull when Summ sits above its own trailing 1-year average
— the operational equivalent of "is breadth better than its recent norm") *does* switch, but
it materially **underperforms buy-and-hold**: CAGR 3.95% vs 10.90%, an excess of **−3.1
bps/day** that clears the Newey-West bar (HAC *t* = **−2.43**) — sitting out of the market
53%/47% costs more of the tape's upward drift than it avoids of the downside.

**Regime-timer shuffled-breadth placebo** (500 draws, time-permute `net_adv`, rebuild the
z-score regime, re-run the backtest): observed HAC *t* = **−2.43** vs two-sided **p = 0.491**
— *half* of randomly re-timed breadth series produce an excess *t* this extreme or worse.
**The negative excess is not a real anti-signal either** — it is the generic cost of any
part-time long/flat filter giving back drift on an upward-drifting tape (the same "beta
trap" sibling study 491 documents for the oscillator's own single-day trigger), not evidence
that the Summation Index's specific temporal path is informative in *either* direction.

## Robustness — EMA spans and basket composition

| variant | switches | excess (bps/day) | HAC *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| spans 10/20 | 250 | −3.221 | −2.53 |
| spans 19/39 (classic) | 115 | −3.125 | −2.43 |
| spans 25/50 | 99 | −3.032 | −2.37 |
| 5-ticker fallback basket (SPY/QQQ/IWM/DIA/GLD) | 97 | −2.979 | −2.34 |

Every variant lands in the same place: a modestly negative, HAC-significant excess versus
buy-and-hold, with **zero post-warm-up zero-level crosses in every basket tried** (the
5-ticker fallback also shows 0 up / 0 down). The result is not an artefact of one EMA-span
choice or one basket.

## Synthetic positive control — the machinery is unbiased

Deterministic mean-reverting breadth-momentum tape with a scheduled planted regime effect
(knob `edge`); no network. The regime-timer detector must NOT fire on a null world and must
recover a planted regime forecast.

| world | level-regime HAC *t* | z-score-regime HAC *t* |
|---|--:|--:|
| null (edge = 0), **20 seeds** | mean **−0.25** (sd 1.00), \|t\|≥2 in **0/20** | mean **−0.36** (sd 0.94), \|t\|≥2 in **0/20** |
| planted edge = 0.6 (seed 666) | **+10.12** (+14.11 bps/day) | **+4.40** (+6.81 bps/day) |

The detector never fires on the null and lights up sharply on a planted regime effect (both
regime rules). *(A faithful-engine / power check only — never cited in support of the
real-tape stamp.)*

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** The textbook zero-cross regime signal cannot fire even once on 21.4
  years of real tape (0 post-warm-up crosses, in either direction, across every basket and
  EMA-span variant tried) — the claim's central mechanism is structurally inert on this
  proxy. The scale-adapted extreme-threshold crosses show no correctly-signed, Welch-robust
  edge over a drift-matched random-day baseline at any of 4 horizons in either direction (7
  of 8 comparisons indistinguishable from noise; the one exception is negative, the wrong
  sign for the claim), and a shuffled-breadth placebo confirms the breadth path carries no
  information (*p* = 0.309).
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** The only regime rule that actually switches (the z-score
  adaptation, since the textbook zero level never crosses) *underperforms* buy-and-hold by
  −3.1 bps/day (HAC *t* = −2.43, robust across EMA spans and baskets) — but the regime-timer
  placebo (*p* = 0.491) shows this is generic drift give-back from being flat sometimes, not
  a real anti-signal either. No residual edge in any direction once costs and the random-day
  control are applied.
- **"Does the Summation Index's regime read confirm bull/bear turns?" — BUSTED.** The zero
  level never confirms anything (it never crosses); the extreme-threshold analog doesn't beat
  random days; and the regime timer built on it loses to simply holding the index. The
  Summation Index is a smoothed breadth *description*, not a forecasting tool.
